package_info.package_manager: N/A (malicious Windows executables, not a package manager ecosystem)
package_info.why_malicious: Both Bisamware and Chile Locker are ransomware families that encrypt user files, demand ransom for decryption, and employ anti-recovery techniques such as deleting shadow copies. They are distributed via malicious documents exploiting vulnerabilities (Bisamware) or through other unknown vectors (Chile Locker), and their sole purpose is extortion and data destruction.

execution_context.file_location: Malicious Microsoft Word file exploiting CVE-2022-30190 (Follina vulnerability)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: ms-msdt:/id PCWDiagnostic ... (malicious MSDT URI in Word document)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At document open-time, the code abuses the MSDT URI scheme to invoke the Microsoft Support Diagnostic Tool, which downloads and executes a remote payload, leading to ransomware execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate documents should not trigger system diagnostic tools or download and execute remote code.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Word documents do not invoke system-level tools or execute code via URI handlers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: MSDT may be legitimately invoked for troubleshooting by administrators, but not via unsolicited documents.
key_indicators: Remote code execution triggered by document open
No user consent for code execution

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Encrypt files and append .BISAMWARE or .crypt extension
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the ransomware enumerates user files, encrypts their contents, and appends a unique extension (.BISAMWARE or .crypt), rendering them inaccessible without the decryption key.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Mass file encryption with ransom extension is a hallmark of ransomware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not encrypt user files en masse without user intent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Encryption utilities may encrypt files, but only with explicit user action and without ransom demands.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After encrypting files, the ransomware creates a ransom note instructing the victim to contact the attacker via a TOR chat room or site to purchase a decryption key.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Creation of ransom notes demanding payment is a direct indicator of ransomware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not extort users or create threatening ransom notes.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; ransom notes are unique to extortionware.
key_indicators: Instructions to contact attacker via TOR

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After encrypting files, the ransomware executes system commands to delete all Windows shadow copies, preventing recovery of files via built-in backup mechanisms.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deleting shadow copies is a common anti-recovery tactic used by ransomware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not indiscriminately delete system backups.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System administrators may clear shadow copies for maintenance, but not in conjunction with file encryption.
key_indicators: No user consent for backup deletion

attack_chain.action: User opens a malicious Microsoft Word document exploiting CVE-2022-30190 (Follina).
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution and ransomware payload download.

attack_chain.action: Ransomware payload is executed on the victim's machine.
Ransomware encrypts user files and appends a unique extension (.BISAMWARE or .crypt).
Ransomware drops a ransom note instructing the victim to contact the attacker.
Ransomware deletes Windows shadow copies to prevent file recovery.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim cannot restore files from backups; extortion pressure increases.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of ms-msdt URI handler from Office documents
Bulk file encryption with new extensions (.BISAMWARE, .crypt)
Creation of ransom note files in user directories
network_indicators: Outbound connections to TOR network (for ransom payment instructions)
Potential C2 or payload download URLs embedded in malicious documents
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents invoking ms-msdt or other unusual URI handlers, detect mass file renaming/encryption with .BISAMWARE or .crypt extensions, alert on creation of known ransom note filenames, and watch for execution of vssadmin.exe with parameters to delete shadow copies. Network monitoring should flag connections to TOR or suspicious external endpoints following document execution.
